The big change

The same monthly cycle, before and after Fisheye Ops

The account started on email and Excel. In 2026 we built Fisheye Ops around Sela's own situations: late POs, multiple batches, renewals mid-month. Flip the switch.

STEP 1

Who is on payroll this month

manual

A sheet typed by hand from contracts, emails and WhatsApp. Joiners and leavers remembered, not detected.

system

Built from the contract records: start, end, renewal, package. Every Sela contract appears automatically with its stage.

STEP 2

Days, deductions, GOSI

manual

Proration worked out in Excel formulas per person; a mid-month start or exit meant a manual recalculation.

system

30-day proration, deductions and GOSI computed per row. The net amount and "x / 30 days" shown on each line.

STEP 3

Match to the Sela PO

manual

PO numbers searched in mailboxes and matched by hand; a person moving to a new PO needed a manual note.

system

Each contract tied to its PO in the ledger. Missing PO, late PO and over-consumed PO are visible on the row.

STEP 4

Approval from Sela

manual

PDF attached to an email, often held back by mail filters; approvals followed up by phone.

system

Sela managers approve on a secure link with phone verification. No attachments, nothing to block.

STEP 5

Pay, in batches

manual

One cycle. A PO that landed after payday meant waiting for next month's run, and the owed days were tracked by hand.

system

Two to three batches a month. The moment a PO lands, the person is in the next batch with every owed day computed. Approved rows lock and leave the list.

STEP 6

Invoice per PO

manual

Invoice typed in Zoho from the sheet; PO balance checked in a separate Excel.

system

One invoice per PO per month, against the ledger's remaining balance. Credit notes attached in place.

STEP 7

Payments and SOA

manual

Bank credits matched to invoices by hand; the statement of account rebuilt in Excel whenever it drifted.

system

Every payment allocated to its invoice, every invoice to its PO. The statement of account comes straight from the ledger.

STEP 8

Last paid, next month

manual

"Was this person paid for July?" answered from the old sheets. A renewal on a new PO needed a manual check.

system

Last-paid date kept per contract and PO. A new contract shows NEW until its first payment; the old one keeps its history.

Days → a review
was: a payroll sheet built over days of Excel work
now: generated from contracts, checked in a sitting
1 → 2–3 batches
was: one cycle, a late PO = a month's wait
now: PO lands → paid in the next batch, owed days included
Memory → record
was: PO, approval and last-paid in heads and inboxes
now: every figure traceable to a contract and a PO

Fisheye Ops is Fisheye's own operations platform; the Sela-specific features were built during 2026 from cases that came up on this account.

Built for Sela's cases

Features that exist because of this account

Each one came from a real situation on this account.

Case: PO arrives after the person started

Late-PO handling

The row stays on the sheet marked "owed" with the days counted per contract.

Case: renewal on a new PO

Last paid per contract

A renewed contract starts NEW; the previous one keeps its last-paid date.

Case: Sela blocks email attachments

Approval portal with phone verification

Approvers open a link, verify by phone, approve.

Case: salary before the contract is signed

Contract-stage guard

Rows on unsigned contracts are flagged in amber; approving a batch with one triggers a warning.

Case: one invoice per PO per month

Invoice preparation from the sheet

Approved payroll rows become the month's invoice lines per PO, so what Sela is billed matches what was approved.

Case: a person moves to a new PO

Invoices follow the PO

An invoice can be re-pointed to the PO Sela assigns, and credit notes sit on the same record, so the PO balance stays exact.

Case: 205 POs, 90+ people a month

Built for Sela's volume

Approved payroll batches lock so nothing is paid twice, PO updates are applied in bulk, and the Sela payroll sheet exports for Procurement in one click.

In the system

What the automation looks like

Live screens, October 2026, filtered to Sela. Names blurred.

Onboarding

From offer to signed contract, without paper chasing

Documents and signatures come in through the candidate's own phone; each step moves the record forward by itself.

STEP 1

Candidate submits documents

candidate portal

A personal link by WhatsApp or email. The candidate verifies by phone, enters ID / Iqama and IBAN, uploads the copies. Arabic or English.

STEP 2

Contract generated and signed

e-signature flow

The agreement PDF is generated from the record. The candidate downloads, signs, uploads; the status flips to Agreement Signed.

STEP 3

Chased until done

action center

Missing documents and unsigned agreements show up as actions with one-click reminders, so no one starts on site with missing papers.

For Sela

Client portal

A read-only live view for Sela: active workforce, onboarding and Qiwa status per person, start dates, this month's headcount. No pricing, no personal IDs.

For Sela

Compliance watch

Contract end dates, probation ends, missing IBANs and expiring documents surface weeks ahead, so renewals reach Procurement before the PO runs out.

For Sela

Payslips and exports

Payslips per person per month, the Sela payroll sheet as Excel in one click, and a client-view export of open actions for Workforce Management.

The rule we hold to

Salaries go out as soon as the PO is in hand, well before Sela's invoice is paid: Fisheye funds that gap every month. A late PO is paid in the next batch the moment it lands, with the owed days counted per contract.

Every month closes with a reconciliation: who was paid, on which contract, against which PO.

Reports to Sela

Flagged early, so no salary waits

Two reports we send Sela so open POs and renewals are followed up before they turn into late salaries or gaps on site.

To Procurement

Missing-PO report

Every employee working without a PO yet, so Procurement can raise it in time and salaries are paid on schedule.

To Workforce Management

Contract end & renewal report

Contracts ending this month, plus those ending in the next two months, so Workforce Management can follow up renewals with each department ahead of time.

Challenges

The hard moments, and what we did

Dec 202585 joiners in one month plus event crews on days' notice+
Problem

Season peak and the Italian Super Cup at the same time; contracts, GOSI, insurance and bank details needed before the first payroll.

Handled

Batch onboarding with a checklist per person; the Super Cup crew of 26 sourced and contracted in under a week.

OngoingPOs arriving after people had started+
Situation

With fast-moving projects, people were often needed on site before the PO could be issued.

Handled

Payroll moved to 2–3 batches a month so a PO landing mid-month is paid within days. Owed days are tracked per contract in the system, and the PO ledger shows Procurement exactly what each PO owes and from when.

Apr 2026Payments received without invoice references+
Situation

Payments arriving as lump sums across many invoices made the two statements of account drift apart.

Handled

SAR 3.55M matched invoice by invoice together with Sela Finance and a clean SOA agreed. Allocation now lives in the system, so the statement is always current.

2026Approval emails held by mail filters+
Situation

Attachments and links in approval emails were often held by corporate mail filters, slowing approvals.

Handled

Built the client approval portal with phone verification. Approvals happen on a link, recorded with name and time.
